gates.observation: The four datasets represent only three system/configuration pairs because both Light Tunnel datasets use the same standard configuration. The pressure-control pair contains one fixed hatch_0 experiment rather than multiple independently recorded worlds.

Light and Wind Tunnel signal columns are disjoint. The only literal common columns are timestamp, config, counter, flag and intervention. Separating controls from responses requires semantic variable names, protocol SET targets or the published ground-truth graph; pressure-control adds eight PID-specific fields.

wt_walks_v1 has ten random-walk seeds and five repeated waveform runs. lt_walks_v1 contains distinct protocols without matched repeats, lt_interventions_standard_v1 contains intervention environments from one configuration, and wt_pressure_control_v1 contains one experiment. No common train/development/unseen-world split exists across all three configurations.

WT seed counts and regime counts can scale within one Wind Tunnel configuration, but no corresponding scale exists for the Light Tunnel or pressure-control configuration. Row subsampling would not add physical worlds.

Persistence, RLS and autoregressive controls apply to time-series walks, while the Light Tunnel intervention table is i.i.d. and pressure-control exposes a closed-loop PID. A common prediction target or horizon cannot be defined without semantic, configuration-specific routing.

All four pages publish CC BY 4.0, MD5 checksums and immutable experiment descriptions. HEAD requests returned a combined compressed size of 53078674 bytes, so acquisition and storage costs are measurable.
